about.label: about
about.heading: I've spent over a decade on the web; code gets rewritten, teams stay.
paragraphs: Hi, I'm Felipe. I've been building software for the web since 2013. I studied Multimedia Engineering at Universidad Militar Nueva Granada (2007–2012): I started with how things look and found my place in how they work.
I spent almost nine years at Axiacore, first as a developer and then as CTO. There I learned that delivering software depends as much on people and clear priorities as it does on code.

I enjoy working with small teams that own what they ship and watching a developer grow into someone who no longer needs me. I aim to give people context and autonomy, not have the final say on every decision.

now.label: now
now.heading: Learning to build with AI without handing over my judgment.
items: Supporting Grupo ilao's engineering team as we develop its insurance platform.
Bringing AI into everyday development: defining the problem before generating code, validating with tests and reviewing decisions, not just syntax.
Sharing reusable instructions for coding agents based on how we work.

work.label: work
work.heading: Decisions, results and lessons
work.intro: The challenges I took on, what I contributed and what I learned along the way.

roles.title: Tech Lead
roles.challenge: Build an insurance platform with an in-house team to support the group's growth.
roles.did: I lead the team and guide architectural decisions. I prioritize incremental delivery and development practices that make the product easier to maintain and extend.
roles.result: The team built a platform that supports the group's operations and continues to evolve.

roles.title: CTO
roles.challenge: Align a software agency's development, QA and operations teams around shared priorities and delivery practices.
roles.did: I agreed on goals and metrics with the executive team and standardized the delivery process. I established a shared foundation of continuous integration, automated code checks and development environments.
roles.result: Under my technical leadership, the teams delivered products including the Crepes & Waffles online store, the Vertech Worldwide insurance platform and MTS's real estate management platform.

roles.title: Senior Full Stack Developer
roles.challenge: Build custom web platforms for different businesses while mentoring two developers and working directly with the executive team.
roles.did: I built the platforms, ran user tests to guide decisions and supported the team's day-to-day work.
roles.result: In January 2018, I became the company's CTO.

roles.title: Director of Technical Development
roles.challenge: Sites and stores for clients such as Apple and the Centro Chía shopping center, with a two-person team: a frontend developer and me on the backend.
roles.did: I built the backend and defined the deployment process. I also contributed to hiring and training, SEO and A/B testing.
roles.result: I learned to lead a team while staying hands-on, balancing client delivery with mentoring another developer.

roles.title: Web Developer
roles.challenge: Build campaign platforms for Cerveza Águila, Banco Colpatria and Banco de Bogotá with fixed launch dates.
roles.did: I implemented the campaign platforms' backend and interaction tracking.
roles.result: I learned to plan development around a fixed launch date.

roles.title: Web Developer
roles.challenge: My first job in web development.
roles.result: I knew I wanted to pursue a career in web development.

items.title: The simplest thing that solves the whole problem
items.text: I avoid adding complexity without a concrete need. Before introducing an abstraction or another layer, I look for the requirement that justifies it.

items.title: Grow in layers
items.text: I start with a small version that works end to end. I build on that foundation so I can validate each step while preserving what already works.

items.title: Boring technology that works
items.text: I prefer familiar, well-maintained tools over the newest ones: they are easier to keep running and to hand over to whoever comes next. I switch when the problem justifies it, not out of curiosity.

items.title: Decisions for the long term
items.text: When a solution is temporary, I make its limits and when to revisit it explicit. Tests must pass before delivery, and I consider the cost of maintaining code, not just writing it.
